The Quiet History of Lighthouses

Lighthouses have guided ships for more than two thousand years. The Pharos of Alexandria, finished around 280 BC, stood over 100 metres tall and was counted among the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

Keepers

For centuries, keepers trimmed wicks and wound clockwork every few hours through the night. Many stations were so remote that families lived there year-round, with supplies arriving by boat once a month.

Automation

By the late twentieth century almost every lighthouse had been automated. The last staffed lighthouse in the United States, Boston Light, still keeps a ceremonial keeper today.
